num_generators: <int> Total number of thermal generators in the fleet.
num_time_periods: <int> Number of consecutive hourly time periods in the planning horizon.
time_period_hours: <int> Duration of each time period in hours.

generators.type: <str> Technology type of the generator (e.g., gas_ct, gas_cc, coal, steam, nuclear).
generators.p_min: <float> Minimum stable power output in MW when the generator is on.
generators.p_max: <float> Maximum power output in MW when the generator is on.
generators.ramp_up_limit: <float> Maximum increase in power output (MW) allowed from one period to the next while online.
generators.ramp_down_limit: <float> Maximum decrease in power output (MW) allowed from one period to the next while online.
generators.startup_ramp_limit: <float> Maximum power output (MW) the generator can produce in the first period it comes online.
generators.shutdown_ramp_limit: <float> Maximum power output (MW) the generator can produce in the last period before going offline.
generators.min_up_time: <int> Minimum number of consecutive periods the generator must remain on once started.
generators.min_down_time: <int> Minimum number of consecutive periods the generator must remain off once shut down.
generators.no_load_cost: <float> Fixed cost ($) incurred per period whenever the generator is on, independent of power output.

startup_costs.label: <str> Name of the startup cost tier (e.g., hot, warm, cold).
startup_costs.max_downtime_hours: <int or null> Maximum prior downtime (hours) for this tier to apply; null for the final cold tier which has no upper bound.
startup_costs.cost: <float> Cost ($) incurred when the generator starts up under this tier.

production_cost_segments.output_mw_start: <float> Lower power output breakpoint (MW) of this cost segment.
production_cost_segments.output_mw_end: <float> Upper power output breakpoint (MW) of this cost segment.
production_cost_segments.marginal_cost_per_mwh: <float> Marginal cost ($/MWh) for each MW produced within this segment.

generators.initial_status: <int> Initial state of the generator before the planning horizon: positive means it has been on for that many periods, negative means it has been off for that many periods.
generators.initial_power: <float> Power output (MW) of the generator immediately before the planning horizon; zero if the generator was off.

demand: <list[float], length num_time_periods> Electricity demand (MW) that must be met in each time period.
reserve_requirement: <list[float], length num_time_periods> Additional reserve capacity (MW) above demand that must be available from online generators in each time period.
